identity.title: PHIBSS: Unified Scaling Relations of Gas Depletion Time and Molecular Gas Fractions

paper_type_evidence.quote: our new study combines three independent methods of determining molecular gas masses from CO line fluxes, far-infrared dust spectral energy distributions, and ~1mm dust photometry, in a large sample of 1444 star forming galaxies

evidence.quote: The data used in this work comprise a total of 1444 measurements of molecular mass, spanning a wide redshift range z=0 to 4.4

question.value: Do molecular gas masses from CO, Herschel dust SEDs and ~1mm dust photometry follow the same scaling relations of depletion time and gas fraction with redshift, offset from the main sequence and stellar mass, once zero-point offsets are minimized?

evidence.quote: This paper provides an update of our previous scaling relations (Genzel et al. 2015) between galaxy integrated molecular gas masses, stellar masses and star formation rates
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2013.1.00092.S.
CO 1-0, 2-1, 3-2 (and in two cases 4-3) rotational line emission

provided.value: CO detections from PHIBSS1/2, xCOLD GASS and others

evidence.quote: 97 detections of CO 2-1 or 3-2 in main sequence SFGs between z=0.5 and 2.7, as part of the PHIBSS2 survey with the updated IRAM NOEMA interferometer
stacks of z=0.1-1.9 SFGs with deep Herschel PACS/SPIRE spectro-photometry in the COSMOS and GOODS (N/S) fields

what.value: 1mm ALMA dust continuum fluxes/gas masses for 102 detections and 21 stacks

evidence.quote: 102 detections and 21 stacks of z=0.9-4.4 of 850-1300 μm continuum fluxes from recent ALMA observations

external_data_from_literature.citation: Scoville et al. 2016, Dunlop et al. 2017, DeCarli et al. 2016, Barro et al. 2016, Tadaki et al. 2015, 2017

what.value: Herschel FIR SED dust masses from stacks

evidence.quote: In all cases we adopted dust masses from these references, and converted to gas mass as described in Sect 2.1.

external_data_from_literature.citation: Magnelli et al. 2014, Berta et al. 2016, G15, Santini et al. 2014, Béthermin et al. 2015

what.value: alpha_CO metallicity recipe, mass-metallicity relation and CO gas-mass calculation follow G15

evidence.quote: Molecular gas masses are then computed from equation (4) in G15.

what.value: 1mm dust gas masses use Scoville et al. (2016) methodology with Tdust=25 K

evidence.quote: using the methodology and calibration proposed by Scoville et al. (2016) with T dust =25K=const.
We adopt in this study the prescription proposed by S14,

unstated_but_needed: Full online table of 1444 measurements (only 14 rows printed)
Exact fitting code and bootstrap/jackknife details
ALMA data reduction for the 10 ALMA CO detections (Genzel et al. in prep)

method.value: Compile CO, FIR-SED and 1mm gas masses; common ladder SFR/M*, S14 main sequence, alpha_CO and gas-to-dust metallicity corrections

evidence.loc: 3.4 Stellar Masses and Star Formation Rates
evidence.quote: Wherever necessary and possible, we adjusted the stellar masses and SFRs from the literature to the same assumptions.

assumptions.value: Chabrier IMF, flat LCDM Om=0.3, H0=70

evidence.quote: flat Λ CDM Universe with Ω m =0.3 and H 0 =70 km/s/Mpc used throughout this paper

method.value: Multi-parameter linear regression in log space, weighted by inverse square uncertainties, with per-method zero-point corrections

evidence.loc: 4.2 New Results for Depletion Time Scaling Relations
evidence.quote: we employ multi-parameter linear regression fitting in 3-, 4- or 5-space of logarithmic variables

evidence.loc: 4.2 New Results for Depletion Time Scaling Relations
evidence.quote: for quantitative fitting of the data, we employ multi-parameter linear regression fitting in 3-, 4- or 5-space of logarithmic variables (log( 1+z), log 2 (1+z), log δMS, log δM * , log δR e ) using all data points individually, weighted by the inverse square of their uncertainties

validation.value: Random half-splitting bootstrap, jackknife, Monte-Carlo mock tests (Appendix A)

evidence.loc: 4.2 New Results for Depletion Time Scaling Relations
evidence.quote: We determined the uncertainties in Table 3a by splitting the sample randomly into two halves, fitting the parameters

evidence.loc: 4.2.2 Variations of depletion time scale above and below the MS
evidence.quote: t depl ~( sSFR/sSFR (MS)) [-0.44±0.03]

results_numeric.quantity: Number of measurements in final fit

evidence.quote: The final data set used in our global analysis of μ gas thus has 1309 measurements.

findings_qualitative.value: CO, FIR-SED and 1mm dust methods give consistent scaling trends after modest zero-point adjustments (0-0.21 dex).

evidence.quote: if modest (0-0.21 dex) adjustments are made to the zero points of each of the techniques and data sets

claims.hypothesis: Different gas mass methods yield consistent scaling relations
claims.experiment: Joint fits of CO, dust-FIR and dust-1mm samples with zero-point offsets
claims.result: Common slopes Bt=-0.62, Ct=-0.44 with scatter ~0.07-0.1 dex

evidence.quote: all data sets, despite the different techniques and analysis methods used, follow the same scaling trends

claims.hypothesis: tdepl and mu_gas depend on optical size or surface density
claims.experiment: Residual fits vs Re and direct fit vs SFR surface density
claims.finding: No or weak size dependence, but optical sizes may be inadequate

evidence.quote: We find no or only weak correlations of t depl and μ gas with optical size R or surface density once one removes the above scalings

limitations_admitted.value: Optical sizes may not represent molecular/dust radii; low-mass results sensitive to alpha_CO metallicity dependence.

evidence.quote: Optical sizes may not represent the true molecular/dust effective radii

referee_caveats_inferred: Compilation heterogeneity; zero-point offsets are fitted rather than independently calibrated
ALMA is a minor data component
